relevance_note: Multicentre Indian LAD cohort with per-patient supplementary tables; e.g. Table S2 lists ITGβ2 variants per patient ("Direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGβ2 gene revealed 57 disease-causing variants in 105 patients").
method_note: Cohort of 132 LAD patients (127 LAD1, 5 LAD3). The 5 LAD3 patients (FERMT3; P128-P132 in Table S2) are out of scope and get no rows. Rows were built by a Python script that transcribed Supplementary Table S1 (clinical summary, P1-P74) and Table S2 (ITGβ2 variants per patient); I checked the parsed cells against the tables. Table S1 is truncated in the converted file after 60,000 characters: P74's row is cut off after the organisms cell (outcome and ANC missing), and no clinical rows exist for P75-P127. Individuals P75-P125 that appear only in Table S2 get rows with label, variant and diagnosis basis only. LAD1 patients named nowhere individually (e.g. P78, P80-P89) get no rows. Table S2 names 96 distinct ITGβ2 patients, whereas the text says 105 patients had a genetic diagnosis. Spans for table values quote the row from the patient label through the cell; for Table S1's second part the clinical-presentations column is heavily padded, so spans reaching later columns (consanguinity, outcome, organisms) exceed 300 characters. Variant spans quote the Table S2 row from the nucleotide change through the patient cell. Values unescape Markdown (c.322C\>T -> c.322C>T, \* -> *); the spans keep the escapes. Ages in S1 are in months per the column headers (header quoted as a second span); ISO values are decimal months (e.g. P0.03M). Zygosity: the Table S2 legend says '# heterozygous'; '#'-marked entries are recorded heterozygous, and unmarked entries are 'not reported' (the text says 95 patients were homozygous but does not say which). The marks are inconsistent: P23, P63 and P76 carry one #-marked and one unmarked variant, and P19 (c.850G>A, c.1264C>T) and P47 (c.322C>T, c.758G>A) have two unmarked variants. The text says compound heterozygous variants were found in only 10 patients, yet 13 patients carry two variants. Variant type maps the 'Type of Mutation' column: Deletion/Insertion -> other (not derived from HGVS), Frame shift delins -> frameshift. Splice-site rows print IVS notation in the amino-acid column, so protein_hgvs is null for them. 'Novel' in the references column is not taken as a pathogenicity class; '57 disease-causing variants' is a cohort-level statement, so pathogenicity is not reported. The 'Umbilical Cord Separation' column (Yes/No/NA) is not defined as delayed separation, so it is not used: the 'delayed umbilical cord separation' item stays not reported, and no feature rows come from that column. The Family History column is not recorded. The ANC column is not used to judge neutrophilia per patient; leukocytosis is marked observed for everyone from the group statement 'Persistent neutrophilic leukocytosis was the characteristic finding in all patients'. Autoimmune complications are marked excluded from 'it was not observed in our patients'. Feature items were split at commas, and at missing commas where two features run together (e.g. P8 'CNS infection skin rash', P10 'respiratory tract infection bronchopneumonia', P49 'perianal rash recurrent diarrhea'). Fragments that are not features by themselves were left out: P24 'perianal', P39 'Respiratory tract' and 'urinary tract'. Some cells contain 'aeruginosa' where another word seems intended (P16 'aeruginosa region abscess', P35 'Non-pyogenic aeruginosa inflammation'); they are recorded as printed. P35's 'Non-pyogenic' is mapped to absence of pus formation. Checklist mappings are conservative. 'Otitis', 'ear discharge', 'recurrent respiratory tract infections', 'CNS infection', 'laryngotracheobronchitis', 'gum swelling' and 'ulcer(s)' without a qualifier are not mapped to the narrower items. 'Non healing ulcer(s)' and 'delayed wound healing' are mapped to impaired wound healing; 'umbilical sepsis' is mapped to omphalitis; loose stool/motions are mapped to diarrhea. Fungal infections come from the presentations and from fungal organisms (candidiasis, Candida, fungus, Fungal). Other isolated organisms are not recorded as features. Treatment: only BMT from the Outcome column; the 12 HSCT patients are not otherwise identified. P20/P28 functional values come from the Discussion sentence giving each person's CD18 and CD11a expression ('respectively', each named). Country 'India' comes from the cohort description. Prior reports: 30 patients in ref 18 and 4 of the c.1224+4A>G LAD1+ patients in ref 39; which individuals were previously reported is not stated. In the reference list, ref 18 is Madkaikar 2015 (PMID:25703682) and ref 39 is Madkaikar 2015 (PMID:25876705).
